about.title: Personal Injury Help in Hawthorne, California
about.longDescription: Hawthorne sits in the South Bay corner of Los Angeles County, and its streets carry a steady flow of daily traffic. Prairie Avenue, El Segundo Boulevard, Rosecrans Avenue and 120th Street all run through neighborhoods where people live, shop and commute. In 2025, the most recent final year of public records, Hawthorne logged 328 injury collisions. Those crashes injured 416 people and took 3 lives. The same records show reports peaking on Fridays between 3 p.m. and 5 p.m. Behind each of those numbers is someone trying to figure out what comes next: an ER bill, a totaled car, time away from work. That is where we come in. We handle personal injury claims in Hawthorne and throughout Los Angeles County. Whether you were hurt behind the wheel, on a bike, on foot, or on someone else's property, you can find out where you stand before deciding anything.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for You in Hawthorne

items.title: The clock runs two years
items.desc: California gives most injured people two years from the date of injury to file a claim. If a city, county or state agency is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months.

items.title: Being partly at fault does not end your claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. Your recovery may be reduced by your share of responsibility, but it is not wiped out just because you were partly to blame.

items.title: No cap on pain and suffering in ordinary cases
items.desc: California does not limit non-economic damages in typical injury claims. That means the toll on your daily life can be counted, not just your medical bills.

items.title: No attorney fee unless you recover
items.desc: We work on contingency. You pay nothing up front, and if there is no recovery there is no attorney fee.

items.question: Where do collisions tend to happen in Hawthorne?
items.answer: Public collision records list Prairie Avenue, El Segundo Boulevard, Rosecrans Avenue and 120th Street as the corridors with the highest counts in Hawthorne. These are simply the busiest reporting locations, not a judgment about any particular road. In 2025 the city recorded 328 injury collisions overall, with reports tending to peak Friday afternoons between 3 and 5.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in California?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims, California allows two years from the date you were hurt. Claims against a government entity often have a much shorter deadline, sometimes six months. Because these windows vary, it helps to talk with an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if the crash was partly my fault?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so partial responsibility reduces what you can recover but does not bar you from recovering. For example, if you are found 20 percent at fault, your recovery would be reduced by that share. An attorney can explain how this might apply to your situation.

items.question: What will an attorney cost me?
items.answer: We work on contingency. There is no upfront fee, and if your case does not result in a recovery, you owe no attorney fee.
